name: los_angeles_basin
rationale: A coastal basin walled by relief on two sides: the Pacific shore and Santa Monica Bay on the south-west, the Santa Monica Mountains (to ~1,000 m) across the north-west, the Palos Verdes rise in the south, and the San Gabriel front (to ~1,700 m within the box) along the north-east, with the flat basin and a dense downtown between them. Chosen to exercise onshore coastal flow, basin routing, terrain masking from real ridgelines, and -- for the wind work that consumes this theatre -- mountain-wave and rotor geometry on the lee of the east-west ranges, none of which the shipped checkpoint has seen. Inside USGS 3DEP coverage, so the DEM is public-domain 3DEP bare earth. The threat field over this AOI is randomly spawned and parameterised exactly as it is everywhere else in the project; nothing here models any real air-defence disposition, and the guardrail in docs/DATA.md applies unchanged.
bounds_policy: A broad civilian coastal-basin-foothill test envelope, about 57 x 56 km, not centred on any site: shoreline, the basin floor, downtown, and ranges to the north and north-east that give 1.7 km of relief for masking and wave scenarios, wide enough for procedurally generated threats and multi-leg missions. Downtown Los Angeles is a high-resolution urban sub-box inside it, not the AOI. The south edge (33.80 N) stops north of the port basins and the naval installations on the southern coast; the east edge keeps the western San Gabriel front. It is not an airport, port or sensitive-site study: civil airfields and restricted property it does contain are protected zones kept clear of extracted geometry, camera framing and every presentation effect. Bounds are fixed here and recorded in the env.aoi component; changing them changes the AOI fingerprint and invalidates every cached artifact keyed to it.

protected_zones.name: civil airport operating area (south-west)
protected_zones.reason: Civil aviation infrastructure. Kept clear of extracted geometry and every presentation effect, so nothing can read as happening at an airport. Camera framing is not restricted here: at city scale a 30 km, 110 degree cone around any downtown shot would contain it, so the zone is protected by extraction and the render cut-out instead.

notes: Civil airfields inside the box come from OurAirports and are start geometry only; the env spawns procedurally and never reads them for placement. The urban_physics box (Downtown Los Angeles) is the only place physics-grade urban obstacles exist; everywhere else the DEM is the whole physical surface.
